turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words are laced with malice, Sandip, and I will not be swayed by them. I will not stand idly by while my people are oppressed. I demand that you cease your harassment and leave my territory immediately.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's to become of you, if I do leave? Will you, with your empty threats, manage to govern this land without the weight of our zamindari's presence?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not concerned with governing the land in your absence, Sandip. My concern is the well-being and safety of my people, and I will take whatever measures are necessary to ensure that.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, how touching, Nikhil, to see you so concerned about the well-being of your people. Tell me, have you considered that perhaps your own brand of governance is what's causing them to suffer?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be lectured on governance by one who has brought nothing but strife and discord to this region, Sandip.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I couldn't help but wonder, Nikhil, what specific actions you believe Sandip's zamindari is taking that warrants such drastic measures.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And I'm sure it's nothing to do with your own petty squabbles with me, Nikhil, but rather a genuine concern for your people's safety. I assure you, my presence here is the only thing holding this place together.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your mocking, Sandip. The local Mussulmans have been making overtures towards me, and I will not ignore their threats.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I'm shaking in my boots, Nikhil, at the thought of these brave Mussulmans threatening you. Do tell, what exactly have they threatened to do to you, apart from stealing the limelight with your own ineptitude?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I've noticed that the local Mussulmans seem to be taking great interest in the zamindari's affairs. Can you tell me more about their concerns, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your frivolous remarks, Sandip. The Mussulmans have been making overtures towards me, and I will not ignore their threats. I will not be deterred by your mocking or your attempts to belittle my concerns.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare us the theatrics, Nikhil. If the Mussulmans were genuinely concerned, wouldn't they be talking to me directly, rather than whispering sweet nothings into your ear?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I assure you, Sandip, that the Mussulmans are not to be underestimated. Their interests are not to be taken lightly, and I will not be party to any actions that may be perceived as provocative.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Really, Nikhil, you're not suggesting that I should be quaking in fear at the thought of these brave Mussulmans, are you? After all, I have a whole army of loyal peasants at my beck and call.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in petty squabbles with you, Sandip, but I warn you: the Mussulmans' actions must be taken seriously, lest we suffer the consequences of their wrath.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I'm shaking in my boots, Nikhil. Tell me, have the Mussulmans threatened to send their most ferocious warrior, the great Khan Bahadur, to put an end to my lordship?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have no reason to believe that the Khan Bahadur will be involved in any potential conflict, but I do know that the Mussulmans are seeking to assert their dominance in this region.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps Nikhil's warning is not something to be dismissed so lightly. Have you considered the impact of such actions on our people and our land?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, always so concerned about the welfare of our people, but where was that concern when Nikhil here was busy exploiting our peasants to line his own pockets?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I have always believed that a zamindar's primary responsibility is to his people, not just to his own interests. Nikhil's warning should be a reminder of the delicate balance we must maintain.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
